literature_structure: Use diminishing returns and recipient-capacity-dependent saturation only; no empirical coefficient is calibrated from historical Afghanistan.

definitions.T: offered foreign training+organizational support resources in one cycle
definitions.A_i: domestic absorptive score = 0.35*security + 0.35*integrity + 0.30*legitimacy, reusing state_regeneration weights
definitions.p_i: offered capacity potential = (0.0048/N)*(T/T_ref), preserving the legacy .0048/N scale when T=T_ref
definitions.G_i: absorbed foreign capacity gain = H_i*(1-exp(-p_i/H_i)) for H_i>0, else 0

properties: For p_i << H_i, G_i approximately equals p_i: low-dose response is locally linear.
G_i is bounded above by H_i: aid volume cannot create unlimited institution capacity in one cycle.
Lower domestic absorptive capacity lowers H_i and therefore lowers the aid saturation point.
No new fitted rate parameter is introduced: r and absorptive weights reuse the domestic state-regeneration architecture.
Existing intervention crowding-out remains a separate subtractive channel; once absorbed gains saturate, crowding-out can produce zero or negative marginal returns.
compatibility: Implement only behind an explicit theory-version/config gate. Legacy foreign-affairs equations remain available for archived parity/revalidation runs.
next_synthetic_test: Before production promotion, compare legacy vs candidate across aid-intensity x host-capacity x crowding-out factorial. Require low-dose continuity, monotone saturation without crowding-out, earlier saturation at lower A_i, and possible inverted-U only when crowding-out is enabled.
guard: Candidate mathematical architecture only. It is not yet a validated Pineland mechanism and makes no empirical claim about a real country.
